invariant: INV-10: a tenant that could not be verified is not a verified tenant
expected: A tenant whose chain could not be checked would be counted sound, so an unverifiable estate would report a clean day.
kills: counts a tenant it could not check as unchecked

invariant: INV-10: a sweep that enumerated nothing has verified nothing
expected: A failure to read the register would return an empty, sound-looking report instead of rejecting.
kills: refuses to report a clean run when the register cannot be read

invariant: INV-10: every registered tenant is walked
expected: Only the first page of tenants would ever be verified; the rest would be silently skipped.
kills: walks every tenant across page boundaries

invariant: Bounded work: a caller cannot request an unbounded or empty page
expected: A page size of 0 or 1001 would be accepted, yielding an empty or oversized sweep.
kills: rejects a page size outside the reviewed bounds

invariant: INV-10: 'not verified' must never read as 'nothing wrong'
expected: A report with unchecked tenants would be declared sound.
kills: counts a tenant it could not check as unchecked

invariant: INV-10: a deleted head is a finding, not a tenant leaving the worklist
expected: Deleting a tenant's chain head would remove it from the sweep entirely and report success.
find:
SELECT r.tenant_id AS organisation_id, r.tenant_id AS id
  FROM audit_chain_registry r
  WHERE p_after IS NULL OR r.tenant_id > p_after
  ORDER BY r.tenant_id
replace:
SELECT h.organisation_id AS organisation_id, h.organisation_id AS id
  FROM audit_heads h
  WHERE p_after IS NULL OR h.organisation_id > p_after
  ORDER BY h.organisation_id
kills: still covers a tenant whose chain head was deleted

invariant: INV-10: a chain registration cannot be removed
expected: Deleting a register row would hide that tenant's chain from every future sweep.
find:
CREATE TRIGGER audit_chain_registry_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON audit_chain_registry
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.reject_registry_mutation();
kills: rejects a privileged DELETE and UPDATE

invariant: Bounded work: a page is capped however much the caller asks for
expected: A caller could request the entire register in one call, unbounded.
kills: caps a page at the reviewed maximum

invariant: INV-10: registration cannot be forgotten
expected: A new tenant would never be registered, so its chain would never be verified.
find:
CREATE TRIGGER organisations_register_audit_chain AFTER INSERT ON organisations
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.register_audit_chain();
kills: is filled by the trigger, not by the caller remembering

invariant: INV-01/least privilege: the runtime role has no grant on the register
expected: `moin_app` could select and join the tenant register directly instead of a capped identifier list.
find: REVOKE ALL ON audit_chain_registry FROM moin_app, moin_provisioner;
replace:
REVOKE ALL ON audit_chain_registry FROM moin_app, moin_provisioner;
GRANT SELECT ON audit_chain_registry TO moin_app;
kills: cannot be enumerated unelevated

invariant: QG-09: the catalog check asserts the register's guard from pg_catalog
expected: A disabled or dropped register guard would pass CI.
kills: rejects a disabled and a dropped register guard

invariant: QG-09: the catalog check asserts the registration trigger
expected: A dropped registration trigger would pass CI while new tenants went unverified.
kills: rejects a dropped and a disabled chain-registration trigger

invariant: QG-09: every reviewed SECURITY DEFINER is pinned by signature, owner, path and grants
expected: The claim function could be downgraded to SECURITY INVOKER, or regranted, without CI noticing.
kills: rejects the claim function changed to SECURITY INVOKER

invariant: Operability: a break and an incomplete run are different incidents
expected: A database outage would page someone for suspected tampering.
kills: raises a SEV2 alarm with its runbook and a distinct exit code

invariant: Operability: a broken chain is SEV2
expected: An integrity break would be routed as a low-severity alert.
kills: raises a SEV2 alarm with its runbook and a distinct exit code

invariant: INV-10: a sweep that could not run exits non-zero
expected: A sweep that never enumerated a tenant would exit 0.
kills: reports a failure rather than a clean run when it cannot enumerate tenants

invariant: INV-12: no personal data or driver text on the log stream
expected: A database error message — which routinely quotes its input — would be written to the alarm line.
kills: emits only the reviewed non-personal fields on every line kind

invariant: Operability: every alarm names its runbook
expected: A SEV2 integrity alarm would arrive with no runbook to follow.
kills: raises a SEV2 alarm with its runbook and a distinct exit code

invariant: INV-10: a broken chain exits non-zero
expected: A run that found a broken chain would exit 0.
kills: raises a SEV2 alarm with its runbook and a distinct exit code

invariant: INV-12: the only string-valued argument kind is `uuid`
expected: A business name or any other free text stored as an argument would pass unreported.
kills: a name, which no pattern would predict

invariant: INV-10: every stored argument key is on the reviewed allowlist
expected: A key that never passed the writer — a restore, a bulk import — would pass unreported.
kills: a key that never passed the writer at all

invariant: QG-09: the argument registry's value kinds cannot be widened silently
expected: A migration adding a free-text value kind would turn the audit trail into a text sink unreported.
kills: a value kind the registry was widened to accept

invariant: INV-12: validation values are bounded scalars
expected: A validation entry carrying text would pass unreported.
kills: a validation entry carrying something other than a bounded scalar

invariant: INV-12: a contact detail is named as such
expected: An email or phone number in an argument would be reported only as generic free text.
kills: a contact detail, named as such

invariant: INV-12: the check never prints the value it found
expected: The check itself would write the personal data it detected into CI logs.
replace: 'printing it would be the leak: ' + row.value
kills: a name, which no pattern would predict

invariant: INV-10: a chain head may only advance by one
expected: Setting `last_seq = 0` would silence verification for that tenant with every event still in place.
find:
OR NEW.last_seq < OLD.last_seq
    OR NEW.last_seq > OLD.last_seq + 1
kills: detects a head rolled back to zero

invariant: INV-10: nothing exists beyond the head unreported
expected: A forged insert past the head, or a rolled-back head, would verify as sound.
kills: detects a head rolled back to zero

invariant: INV-10: an event may only be inserted correctly linked to the head
expected: A privileged direct INSERT could place an unlinked forged event in the trail.
find:
CREATE TRIGGER audit_events_linked_only BEFORE INSERT ON audit_events
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.reject_unlinked_audit_event();
kills: detects a forged event written past the head

invariant: INV-10: TRUNCATE is refused on the audit tables
expected: `TRUNCATE audit_events` would erase the whole trail and the next sweep would report it clean.
find:
CREATE TRIGGER audit_events_no_truncate BEFORE TRUNCATE ON audit_events
  FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION app.reject_audit_mutation();
kills: refuses TRUNCATE on the register

invariant: INV-10: TRUNCATE is refused on the register
expected: Emptying the register would take every tenant off the worklist at once.
find:
CREATE TRIGGER audit_chain_registry_no_truncate BEFORE TRUNCATE ON audit_chain_registry
  FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION app.reject_registry_mutation();
kills: refuses TRUNCATE on the register

invariant: INV-10: the register is reconciled against an independent witness
expected: A tenant provisioned but never registered would be invisible to the sweep forever.
replace:
const unregisteredTenants: readonly string[] = [];
  void unregistered;
kills: reports a provisioned tenant that never reached the register

invariant: INV-10: an unregistered tenant is never 'sound'
expected: A sweep would report a clean estate while a tenant sat outside it.
kills: reports a provisioned tenant that never reached the register

invariant: INV-10/INV-17: the register covers tenants that predate it
expected: Every tenant existing when the migration landed would be permanently unverifiable.
find: INSERT INTO audit_chain_registry(tenant_id) SELECT id FROM organisations ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
kills: registers every pre-existing organisation

invariant: INV-10: guards are ENABLE ALWAYS, not origin-only
expected: `session_replication_role = 'replica'` would bypass every append-only guard with no schema change.
kills: rejects a disabled mutation guard

invariant: QG-09: a reviewed function's body is pinned, not only its identity
expected: A guard could be replaced with one that returns without raising, keeping name, owner and triggers.
kills: rejects a guard whose body was replaced

invariant: QG-09: CI fails on a register that misses a provisioned tenant
expected: A registration gap would pass CI even after the trigger was put back.
kills: rejects a register that does not account for every provisioned tenant

invariant: INV-01: the scanner reads under tenant scope as the runtime role
expected: FORCE RLS would return zero rows and the check would report a clean trail having inspected nothing.
find: const counted = await client.query<{ n: string }>(EVENT_COUNT_QUERY);
replace: const counted = await pool.query<{ n: string }>(EVENT_COUNT_QUERY);
kills: a name, which no pattern would predict

invariant: INV-10: a scan that inspected nothing is not a clean scan
expected: A vacuous scan would print a reassuring sentence and exit 0.
kills: refuses to pass when tenants exist but it inspected no events

invariant: INV-12: an argument key is not printed unless its shape is safe
expected: A forged key that is itself personal data would be written into CI logs by the check.
kills: a forged argument key that is itself personal data

invariant: INV-12: operation and target_kind shapes are asserted
expected: A dropped column CHECK would let free text into retained, un-erasable columns unreported.
kills: an operation or target kind that only a dropped CHECK could have allowed

invariant: INV-10: a sweep of zero tenants is not a clean day
expected: A truncated or unreadable register would exit 0, indistinguishable from a healthy estate.
kills: exits non-zero on a sweep of zero tenants

invariant: Operability: the unchecked alarm carries a SQLSTATE
expected: Every database failure would emit the same useless reason, since `pg` sets `name` to 'error'.
find:
const code = (error as { code?: unknown } | null)?.code;
  if (typeof code === 'string' && /^[0-9A-Z]{5}$/u.test(code)) return code;
kills: emits only the reviewed non-personal fields on every line kind

invariant: INV-10: coverage is a property of the register, not of the worklist drained from it
expected: A deadline expiring between pages would report `unreached: 0` and a sound sweep, having verified one tenant out of many.
kills: does not call a deadline-truncated sweep sound

invariant: INV-10: a sweep that did not reach the end of the register is not sound
expected: An incomplete sweep would be declared sound despite reporting a shortfall.
kills: treats a shortfall it could not count as incomplete

invariant: INV-10: not knowing whether coverage was complete is not the same as it being complete
expected: If the shortfall could not be counted, the sweep would claim complete coverage.
kills: treats a shortfall it could not count as incomplete

invariant: Operability: an incomplete sweep exits non-zero
expected: A deadline-truncated sweep would exit 0, so the schedule would record a clean day.
kills: fails when it cannot even establish whether coverage was complete

invariant: INV-10: the scanner reconciles its coverage against the provisioning witness
expected: A tenant provisioned but absent from the register would be outside the scan, and a planted leak under it would go unreported.
find: const missing = await pool.query<{ id: string }>(UNREGISTERED_QUERY, [UNREGISTERED_SAMPLE]);
replace: const missing = { rows: [] as { id: string }[] };
kills: fails when a provisioned tenant hides a leaking argument outside the register

invariant: Operability: the scanner names the coverage gap, not just a finding count
expected: An operator would see a list of findings with no statement that whole tenants were never reached.
kills: fails when a provisioned tenant hides a leaking argument outside the register

invariant: INV-10/INV-12: a stored value must match its registered kind's JSON type
expected: A `uuid`-kind argument holding a boolean or a number would produce no finding at all.
kills: catches a uuid kind holding a boolean

expected: Value validation would be skipped entirely: a non-UUID string under a `uuid` kind, and any out-of-bounds count, would pass.
kills: a name, which no pattern would predict

invariant: INV-10: an argument kind with no validator fails closed
expected: A kind the check cannot validate would be silently accepted, so widening the registry would bypass the scanner.
kills: fails closed on a registered kind it has no validator for

invariant: INV-10: 'head absent' and 'event exists' come from one snapshot
expected: A legitimate first append committing mid-verification would be reported as `missing-head` — a false integrity alarm on a sound chain.
kills: does not report missing-head when a first append commits mid-verification

invariant: INV-10: events without a head are a break
expected: Fixing the false alarm by suppressing the real one: an orphaned trail with no head would verify as sound.
kills: still detects a genuine orphan event with no head

invariant: INV-10: a sweep's population is bounded by the high-water mark captured at its start
expected: The sweep would chase registrations that land while it runs, so on a busy estate it would never terminate and its verdict would cover an ever-shifting population.
find:
AND r.registration_seq <= coalesce(p_high_water, 0)
  ORDER BY r.registration_seq
kills: reads the high-water mark once, not once per page

invariant: INV-10: the high-water mark is read once per sweep, not once per page
expected: The population would grow underneath the sweep meant to be bounded by it, so 'complete coverage' would mean nothing.
kills: reads the high-water mark once, not once per page

invariant: INV-10: paging follows registration order, which UUID order does not encode
expected: The original defect: a registration landing behind the cursor would be invisible to the sweep and to its shortfall count, and a half-covered estate would report sound.
find:
SELECT r.tenant_id AS organisation_id, r.tenant_id AS id, r.registration_seq
  FROM audit_chain_registry r
  WHERE r.registration_seq > coalesce(p_after, 0)
replace:
SELECT r.tenant_id AS organisation_id, r.tenant_id AS id,
         (row_number() OVER (ORDER BY r.tenant_id))::bigint AS registration_seq
  FROM audit_chain_registry r
  WHERE r.registration_seq > coalesce(p_after, 0)
kills: is verified before coverage is complete, whatever its UUID sorts like

invariant: INV-10: a deadline shortfall is counted inside the captured population
expected: A deadline would end the sweep and declare complete coverage, because nothing would check how much of the population was left.
kills: reports the snapshot shortfall and is not sound

invariant: INV-10: the scanner scans exactly the population it captured

invariant: INV-10: the scanner traverses the register population as well as reconciling it

kills: a late registration behind the cursor is excluded by the bound, not skipped by ordering

invariant: A registration's position in the population order is assigned once and strictly advances

find:
ALTER TABLE audit_chain_registry
  ADD CONSTRAINT audit_chain_registry_registration_seq_key UNIQUE (registration_seq);
kills: refuses two registrations sharing a position

expected: A caller able to rewrite a sequence could move a tenant out of the current population, which is the UUID-cursor defect made deliberate.
